Citrus bergamia, also known as bergamot, has been found to improve skin health by reducing oxidative damage and enhancing cellular renewal. Its bioactive compounds, such as flavonoids, contribute to a brighter, more youthful complexion. benefits.constituents: Citrus bergamia improves skin health because it contains bioactive constituents such as flavonoids and alkaloids. Additionally, they may help regulate sebum production, preventing acne and maintaining a balanced skin microbiome. Overall, the combination of these natural compounds supports a healthier, more radiant complexion.
benefits.study: According to "Zhongguo Zhong yao za zhi = Zhongguo zhongyao zazhi = China journal of Chinese materia medica", Citrus bergamia, specifically bergamot, was found to improve skin health by increasing the activity of superoxide dismutase, enhancing collagen content, and decreasing malondialdehyde levels in mice.

Citrus bergamia, also known as bergamot, has been studied for its potential to lower blood pressure due to its rich content of flavonoids and other bioactive compounds. These compounds may help relax blood vessels and improve circulation, thereby supporting cardiovascular health.
benefits.constituents: Citrus bergamia lowers blood pressure because it contains bioactive constituents such as flavonoids and alkaloids. These compounds have been shown to improve endothelial function and reduce oxidative stress. The polyphenols in bergamot help relax blood vessels, promoting better blood flow. Additionally, they may inhibit the enzyme angiotensin-converting enzyme, which is involved in blood pressure regulation. Studies suggest that regular consumption of citrus bergamia can contribute to maintaining healthy blood pressure levels.

benefits.constituents: Citrus bergamia lowers cholesterol because it contains bioactive constituents such as flavonoids and alkaloids.
